extracted.intended_audience: users/developers of the PARI/GP library (mathematicians, number theorists, scientific programmers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP arithmetic and character-related library functions, describing each routine's purpose, return values, options, edge-cases, and example usage. Intended to guide correct calling and interpretation of results when using PARI/GP.

rubrics_metrics.name: bestapprPade
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a best rational approximation (Padé approximation) to a power series or similar object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies recursively to components of complex objects (polynomials, vectors, ...). If rational reconstruction fails for any single entry, returns []. Example: T = 1 + x + x^2 + ... + O(x^7); bestapprPade(T) => 1/(-x + 1). Library syntax: GEN bestapprPade(GEN x, long B).

rubrics_metrics.name: bezout / gcdext (alias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated alias bezout(x,y) for gcdext: extended gcd routines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gcdext0(GEN x, GEN y). (No further detail in chunk.)

rubrics_metrics.name: bigomega(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of prime divisors of the integer |x| counted with multiplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: factor(392) => [[2,3],[7,2]]; bigomega(392) => 5; omega(392) => 2 (without multiplicity). Library syntax: long bigomega(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: charconj(cyc, chi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the conjugate character of a character on a finite abelian group represented by its elementary divisors (or any object with a .cyc method).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters are row vectors [a1,..,an] with evaluation exp(2πi * aj*nj/dj). Works with znstar and bnrinit outputs. Examples: cyc=[15,5], chi=[1,1] => [14,4]. For Dirichlet characters (cyc = znstar(q,1)) Conrey representations are available (see character section). Library syntax: GEN charconj0(GEN cyc, GEN chi). Also GEN charconj(GEN cyc, GEN chi) when types are known (no checks).

rubrics_metrics.name: chardiv(cyc, a, b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two characters a and b of the same abelian group, return the quotient character a/b = a * b^{-1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts cyc as elementary divisors or objects with .cyc. For Dirichlet characters, multiple representations (standard vector, Conrey label, Conrey logarithm) exist; if formats differ, a Conrey logarithm is used for the result. Examples show mixed-format handling. Library syntax: GEN chardiv0(GEN cyc, GEN a, GEN b) and GEN chardiv(GEN cyc, GEN a, GEN b) when checks can be skipped.

rubrics_metrics.name: chareval(G, chi, x, {z})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the value of a character chi at an element x of an abelian group G which affords discrete logarithm (e.g., G = znstar(N,1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Note explains representation via a morphism c : G → Z/oZ with ζ an o-th root of unity and how chi(gi) = ζ^{ci(o/oi)}. For Dirichlet characters there are three formats (t_VEC, t_COL Conrey, t_INT Conrey label). Behavior depends on optional z:
- omitted: return rational number c(x)/o for x coprime to conductor, else sentinel -1.
- z integer o: return integer c(x) when x in group else -1.
- z = [zeta,o]: return ζ^{c(x)} if x in group else 0 (extends Dirichlet/Hecke characters to Z/ideals).
- z = [vzeta,o]: vzeta is precomputed table of powers, used for table lookup; sentinel 0 if not in group.
Library syntax: GEN chareval(GEN G, GEN chi, GEN x, GEN z = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: chargalois(cyc, {ORD})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return representatives for the Galois orbits of complex characters of a finite abelian group represented by elementary divisors (or objects with .cyc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional ORD filters by character orders: if ORD is int, restrict to orders < ORD; if ORD is vector, restrict to listed orders. Example: chargalois(znstar(96)) -> 16 orbits; chargalois(G,4) -> orders < 4. Given character of order n, orbit contains φ(n) characters. Library syntax: GEN chargalois(GEN cyc, GEN ORD = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: charker(cyc, chi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the kernel of the character chi as a matrix in Hermite Normal Form (HNF) which is a left-divisor of matdiagonal(d) where d are the elementary divisors; columns express subgroup generators in terms of group generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determinant of the returned matrix is the kernel index. Works with Dirichlet characters and Conrey representations. Example outputs shown; library syntax: GEN charker0(GEN cyc, GEN chi) and GEN charker(GEN cyc, GEN chi) when no checks needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: charmul(cyc, a, b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two characters a and b of a finite abelian group, return their product character ab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts cyc as elementary divisors or objects with .cyc. For Dirichlet characters multiple representations exist; if formats differ a Conrey logarithm is used. Examples illustrate mixed-format handling. Library syntax: GEN charmul0(GEN cyc, GEN a, GEN b) and GEN charmul(GEN cyc, GEN a, GEN b) when safe to skip checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: charorder(cyc, chi)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the order of the character chi (multiplicative order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works with objects having .cyc (e.g., znstar). For Dirichlet characters Conrey representations are supported. Examples show charorder( [15,5], [1,1] ) => 15. Library syntax: GEN charorder0(GEN cyc, GEN chi) and GEN charorder(GEN cyc, GEN chi) when types known.

rubrics_metrics.name: charpow(cyc, a, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given integer n and character a, return the character a^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts cyc as elementary divisors or objects with .cyc. For Dirichlet characters output format follows input format (standard vector, Conrey label, Conrey log). Examples given. Library syntax: GEN charpow0(GEN cyc, GEN a, GEN n) and GEN charpow(GEN cyc, GEN a, GEN n) when no checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: chinese(x, {y})
rubrics_metrics.description: If x and y are both intmods or polmods, create an element congruent to x mod modulus(x) and y mod modulus(y) when possible (Chinese remainder combination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: chinese(Mod(1,2), Mod(2,3)) => Mod(5,6). Works recursively on vectors and matrices (applies to each component). For polynomial arguments in same variable, applied to each coefficient; if degrees differ, higher-degree terms from longer polynomial are copied verbatim (often undesirable) — recommended to convert to equal-length vectors first. If y omitted and x is a vector, chinese applied recursively to components, yielding residue class common to all components. chinese(x,x) = x for all types, enabling vectors to contain arbitrary identical data across the two arguments. Library syntax: GEN chinese(GEN x, GEN y = NULL). Also GEN chinese1(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: content(x, {D})
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the gcd of all coefficients of x when that notion makes sense (polynomial, power series, vector/matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
If x scalar: returns absolute value for rational ints; returns 1 or x for inexact/exact inputs respectively. For rational functions, content = content(numerator)/content(denominator). For recursive structures, when matrix/vector coefficient appears, gcd is taken with its content. t_VECSMALL assumes signed integers. Optional D controls ring/context:
- D = 1: Q-structure only, denominator as positive rational number.
- D = variable (e.g., 'x'): consider entries as rational functions in K(x) and return content in K.
Examples: content(x+1/y+1/2) as POL in x => 1/(2*y); content(...,1) => 1/2. Library syntax: GEN content0(GEN x, GEN D = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: contfrac(x, {b}, {nmax})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the vector of partial quotients of the continued fraction expansion of x; output normalized so last partial quotient = 1 (unless n=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length limited by nmax; if omitted expansion stops at last significant partial quotient. Works for reals, rational functions, power series. If vector b supplied (numerators), numerators equal coefficients of b instead of 1; length equals length of b unless next quotient can't be reliably computed (e.g., remainder zero or under precision bounds). Obsolete hack: contfrac(x, , b) if b integer treats b as nmax. Examples: contfrac(Pi) given. Implementation notes and pseudocode for generalized continued fraction and Engel expansion provided. Library syntax: GEN contfrac0(GEN x, GEN b = NULL, long nmax). Also GEN gboundcf, GEN gcf, GEN gcf2.

rubrics_metrics.name: contfracpnqn(x, {n = -1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given vector/matrix x of partial quotients [a0,..,an] (or generalized continued fraction with two rows), return the 2x2 matrix [pn, pn-1; qn, qn-1] of convergents so pn/qn equals the continued fraction value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If n≥0 present, returns all convergents from p0/q0 to pn/qn (or all convergents if x too small). Examples show computing all convergents from contfrac(Pi). Library syntax: GEN contfracpnqn(GEN x, long n). Also GEN pnqn(GEN x) for n = -1.

rubrics_metrics.name: core(n, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given integer n = d * f^2 with d squarefree, return d (the core). If flag non-zero returns [d,f]. By convention core(0,1) returns [0,1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN core0(GEN n, long flag). Also GEN core(GEN n) with flag=0 and GEN core2(GEN n) for flag=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: coredisc(n, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the unique fundamental discriminant d such that n = d * f^2 with f positive rational. If flag non-zero, also return [d,f].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental discriminant characterization (t ≡ 1 mod 4 or 4t ≡ 8,12 mod 16 with t squarefree). If n ≡ 0 or 1 mod 4, f integer; otherwise f half-integer. Convention: coredisc(0,1) => [0,1]. quaddisc(n) gives same value and works for rational n. Library syntax: GEN coredisc0(GEN n, long flag). Also GEN coredisc(GEN n) and GEN coredisc2(GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: dirdiv(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide two Dirichlet-series-representing vectors x and y (possibly different lengths, with y[1] != 0), returning the quotient series as a vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies coefficient-wise as Dirichlet series quotient. Library syntax: GEN dirdiv(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: direuler(p = a, b, expr, {c})
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the Dirichlet series attached to the Euler product specified by local factor expr(X) as p ranges through primes from a to b; output is vector of series coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: expr must be polynomial or rational function in variable X and interpreted as local factor expr(p^{-s}). If c omitted, output first b coefficients; otherwise output first c coefficients. If c > b computed coefficients include missing Euler factors (zeros) for primes beyond b. Example: direuler(p=2,10, 1/((1-X)*(1-p*X))) computes sigma function coefficients. Library syntax: direuler(void *E, GEN (*eval)(void*,GEN), GEN a, GEN b).

rubrics_metrics.name: dirmul(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiply two Dirichlet-series-representing vectors x and y (possibly different lengths), returning the product series as a vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents multiplication of Dirichlet series ∑ x_n n^{-s} and ∑ y_n n^{-s}. Product length is min(#x * v(y), #y * v(x)) where v(x) is index of first non-zero coefficient. Works recursively; example shows product of Möbius with ones. Library syntax: GEN dirmul(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: divisors(x, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a row vector containing the divisors of x. If flag=1 return pairs [d, factor(d)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisors are products of irreducible factors (no negative exponents). For integers, return positive divisors in increasing order. For polynomials, returns polynomial divisors. Example divisors(12) => [1,2,3,4,6,12]; divisors(12,1) returns [d, factor(d)]. Library syntax: GEN divisors0(GEN x, long flag), and convenience functions GEN divisors(GEN N) and GEN divisors_factored(GEN N) for flag variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: divisorslenstra(N, r, s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given integers N > s > r ≥ 0 with (r, s) = 1 and s^3 > N, find all divisors d of N such that d ≡ r (mod s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are at most 11 such divisors (Lenstra bound). Preconditions are required; if not met result is undefined (may miss divisors). Examples show correct and failing precondition behavior. Library syntax: GEN divisorslenstra(GEN N, GEN r, GEN s).

rubrics_metrics.name: eulerphi(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Euler's totient function φ(|x|) = |(Z/xZ)^*|, with convention φ(0) := 2 so znstar(0).no = eulerphi(0) = 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: eulerphi(40) => 16. Library syntax: GEN eulerphi(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: factor(x, {D})
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor x over domain D (if omitted domain determined from x). Returns two-column matrix: irreducible factors and exponents. For integers includes unit -1 when x<0 and denominators with negative exponents; 0 factored as 0^1; 1 as empty factorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior depends on input type: integers, Gaussian ints, univariate/multivariate polynomials, rationals, p-adics, finite fields, number fields, reals/complex (inexact handling), etc. Large factors >2^64 are pseudoprimes unless factor_proven set; use isprime to verify. Optional int D limits search to primes p < D (useful but may leave large cofactor). Domain D can be specified to set field K (Q, Z/pZ, Fq, number field, Q(i), Q(w), R, C, Qp, etc.). For inexact polynomials, inputs are first rounded to exact then factorization truncated—advice: prefer factoring exact polynomials to avoid pitfalls. Notes re inseparable polynomials, multivariate factoring order (by main variable then degree), and examples for many domains. Deprecated/alternate specialized functions exist (factormod, factormodDDF, factorpadic, nffactor, polroots, polrootsreal). Library syntax: GEN factor0(GEN x, GEN D = NULL) and convenience wrappers GEN factor(GEN x), GEN boundfact(GEN x, ulong lim).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorback(f, {e})
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconstruct the original object from its factorization f (and optional exponents e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If e present, both vectors must have same length and product is ∏ f[i]^{e[i]}. If e omitted and f is a vector, interpret as factors with exponent 1. Special cases: integer 1 corresponds to empty factorization. Examples: factor(12) => [[2,2],[3,1]]; factorback gives 12. Library syntax: GEN factorback2(GEN f, GEN e = NULL) and convenience GEN factorback(GEN f) for e = NULL.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorcantor (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete alias; use factormod.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN factmod(GEN x, GEN p).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorff (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete, kept for backward compatibility; use factormod.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN factorff(GEN x, GEN p = NULL, GEN a = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorial(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factorial: the notation x! returns integer factorial when x integer; factorial(x) returns a real number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mpfactr(long x, long prec) for real factorial; GEN mpfact(long x) returns integer x! as t_INT.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorint(x, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor integer x into product of pseudoprimes using combination of SQUFOF, Pollard Rho (Brent), Lenstra ECM (Montgomery mods), MPQS (LiDIA-adapted), and pure power search. Returns two-column matrix like factor with primes and exponents. By default factors > 2^64 are pseudoprimes (use isprime or set factor_proven to verify).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag bits modify algorithms: 1 avoid MPQS, 2 skip first-stage ECM (may fallback), 4 avoid Rho and SQUFOF, 8 don't run final ECM (may declare huge composite prime). Uses probabilistic primality test; composites might be missed (no known counterexample). Users can tune flags and inspect internals via gp's debug default parameter. Library syntax: GEN factorint(GEN x, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: factormod(f, {D}, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor polynomial f over finite field specified by domain D. D may be prime p (Fp), [T,p] for Fp[x]/(T), a t_FFELT finite-field element, or omitted to factor over field of definition of f (must be finite field). Returns two-column matrix of irreducible polynomials and exponents; canonical ordering by increasing degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coefficients of f must be compatible with the field. If flag non-zero, output only degrees of irreducible polynomials in increasing order (useful for L-functions); degree-list ordering may not correspond to factor order when multiplicities present. Examples illustrate factorings over F3, F9 via different domain specifications, and liftall to view lifted polynomials. Library syntax: GEN factormod0(GEN f, GEN D = NULL, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: factormodDDF(f, {D})
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct-degree factorization of squarefree polynomial f over finite field defined by D: returns factors grouped by irreducible degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D same options as factormod. Result is two-column matrix: first column monic squarefree factors each of whose irreducible factors have degree d, second column the degree d. Faster than full factorization; canonical and ordered by increasing degree. Examples and timing comparisons with full factorization shown. Library syntax: GEN factormodDDF(GEN f, GEN D = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: factormodSQF(f, {D})
rubrics_metrics.description: Squarefree factorization of polynomial f over finite field defined by D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D options as for factormod. Squarefree factorization is faster than full factorization and returns squarefree factors. Works over Fp, extension fields, t_FFELT, or omitted field of definition. (Chunk ends while describing this function; additional details follow in subsequent text.) Library syntax: (implied) GEN factormodSQF(GEN f, GEN D = NULL).
